sections.h2: Where a county deed is filed
sections.html:
A deed for a house in St. Louis County goes to the Recorder of Deeds in Clayton, but only when the parcel lies outside the City of St. Louis. The counter is at 41 South Central Avenue. Call (314) 615-7100. The office is open Monday through Thursday only, from 8 until 3:30.

Besides deeds, the same staff file subdivision plats, federal and state tax liens and other written instruments touching real or personal property, and they issue marriage licenses. Anything recorded there is open to public research. Written questions can go to Recorder@stlouiscountymo.gov or to 41 South Central Avenue, Clayton, MO 63105. For a sale in Florissant, Chesterfield, Ballwin or any other municipality in the county, the closing agent usually carries the signed deed to this office, so a seller seldom visits in person.

sections.h2: What the county charges to record a deed
sections.html:
The county charges $26 for page one and $3 for every page after it. A document that ignores the state layout rules draws a further $25. Anyone who files electronically may pay a vendor's own charges on top.

The layout rules come from RSMo 59.310. A recorder may turn away a paper that fails them, or accept it with the surcharge. A deed packet for this office typically needs:

  • single-sided pages on white or pale paper, loose rather than bound;
  • type of at least eight points, in black or dark ink, with legible signatures and typed names beneath them;
  • three clear inches at the top of the first sheet, reserved for the recorder's certification, and three-quarters of an inch around the other edges;
  • on that first sheet, under the margin: title, date, every grantor with marital status, every grantee, statutory addresses, and the legal description.

If you overpay, a refund check comes back only when the excess tops $10. Smaller overages go into the county's general fund.

They are separate. In 1877 St. Louis voters chose to leave the county, and the two have kept separate land records ever since. A house a few blocks east or west of the boundary can therefore belong to a different office.

The city's recorder works from City Hall, Room 126, at 1200 Market Street, and publishes its own prices. Look at the parcel's address first, because a deed sent to the wrong office will not help your closing.

sections.h2: Mailing a deed or filing it electronically
sections.html:
Mailing works. Send or hand over the original notarized deed, with a check or money order made out to ROD, to the Clayton address. The county returns the original within a week of recording. Electronic filing runs through the third-party vendors listed on the county's e-recording page, and a business that wants to file that way contacts a vendor to set up service.

A seller with a single deed rarely needs that, because the title company handling the sale will normally take care of the recording and pass along a copy. If you wonder whether any charge besides recording applies to your particular deed, ask the Recorder's office at (314) 615-7100 or the closing agent before you sign.

sections.h2: If the recorder rejects your deed
sections.html:
A rejected paper goes back to whoever brought it, with the reason written out. Once the problem is fixed, you can present it again. The same law lets a non-conforming paper be recorded for the $25 add-on instead of being refused.

Some papers are exempt from the layout rules and may still be recorded. The list includes documents signed before January 1, 2002, papers executed outside the United States, certified copies, and anything where an original party has died or is otherwise incapacitated. An heir selling a parent's house could fall into that last group, so tell the title company early.

Hold on to the stamped copy afterward. The top three inches carry the recorder's certification, which makes the copy your proof that the deed reached the record.

sections.h2: Ordering a copy or searching old deeds
sections.html:
You can order a certified copy online from the county's vendor, or go in person. The counter takes cards only. Pages cost $2 for the first and $1 for each after, a typical printed deed comes to $5 plus a convenience charge, and each certification adds $1.

  • The web search reaches recorded deeds through 1974.
  • If you bought before 1974, book an appointment for a deed search in Clayton.
  • You may also book one if you would rather search on site.
  • State law caps what a recorder may charge for a paper copy of a recorded instrument at $2 for the first page and $1 for each later page, which matches the county's copy price.

Pull a recent copy before you list. The buyer's title company will check names and the legal description against it.

St. Louis County lies in eastern Missouri, with the Missouri River along its north edge, the Meramec River along most of the south, and the Mississippi and the City of St. Louis to the east. It has about 990,911 residents on 507.88 square miles of land, and 448,637 homes. Owners live in 69.2% of occupied homes. The typical owned house is valued at $276,800, median household income is $82,936, and median monthly rent is $1,209.

Eighty-seven municipal governments operate in the county, and roughly one resident in three lives in an unincorporated area where the county itself handles zoning and code enforcement. A deed for a house in Clayton and one for a house in Wildwood are filed at the same counter, though each municipality governs its own streets. Ask city hall about local steps before you list.

1. Confirm your parcel is in the county and not the city.
  2. Pull a recent copy of your deed so you can compare names and the legal description with the sale contract.
  3. Let the title company prepare the new deed, or check the layout rules above if you prepare your own.
  4. Plan any in-person trip for Monday through Thursday, before 3:30.
  5. After recording, keep the stamped copy.

A sale to a cash buyer goes through the same recording steps, so the same fees and layout rules apply. The difference is speed: with no lender involved, the deed can often be signed and sent to Clayton sooner after the closing date is set.

faqs.q: Where do I find the St. Louis County recorder?
faqs.a: At 41 South Central Avenue in Clayton, MO 63105. Call (314) 615-7100 or write to Recorder@stlouiscountymo.gov. The doors are open Monday to Thursday from 8 to 3:30.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge for a deed here?
faqs.a: Twenty-six dollars for the first page and three for each page that follows, with a $25 add-on for a paper that breaks the Missouri format rules. Vendors who handle e-recording can charge extra.

faqs.q: Will the county take a deed by post?
faqs.a: Yes. Mail the original notarized deed and a check or money order payable to ROD to the Clayton office. The county returns the original within a week of recording.

faqs.q: My house is in St. Louis city. Do I file in Clayton?
faqs.a: No. The City of St. Louis keeps its own land records at City Hall, Room 126, and charges its own prices. Clayton handles only parcels in the county.

faqs.q: How far back does the online deed search go?
faqs.a: Recorded deeds can be searched through 1974. A property bought before that year calls for an appointment at the Clayton office.
